description.narrative:
Advancing Transitional Justice in Syria.
Objective 1: Operationalize and Strengthen Transitional Justice Institutions ICTJ will support the Commission on the Missing and Forcibly Disappeared and the Commission on Transitional Justice alongside a wider set of emerging bodies and justice-related mechanisms to facilitate that their work is transparent, victim-centered, and able to function effectively under difficult conditions through expert help in developing road maps and other tools, capacity building workshops, and sharing of comparative lessons from other countries, amongst other.
Objective 2: Establish an Expert Resource and Working Group The working group will provide a standing platform for Syrian institutional leaders, ministries, and international counterparts to exchange knowledge, align strategies, and maintain political momentum for transitional justice. It will deliver structured advice on relevant topics, draft recommendations, and share comparative insights from other transitional contexts to guide institutional development and policymaking.
Objective 3: Support for Civil Society Organizations Building on its long-standing relationships, ICTJ will deepen partnerships with networks such as Bridges of Truth and the Association of Detainees and the Missing in Sednaya Prison (ADMSP), while also engaging a wider range of grassroots groups. The initiative will provide targeted subgrants, training, and technical accompaniment to strengthen civil society’s ability to advocate effectively, contribute to policy debates, and engage directly with transitional justice institutions.
The partner emphasizes the inclusion of women in these processes.
